resources.string: Where this day happened. The diary has no internet and doesn\'t know where you are, so you write the place yourself.
Both pages of this day are full
Voice can\'t be recorded without microphone permission
Diaries will stand on a shelf. Without a name it\'s simply “Diary”.
Tap a spine to take the diary out. Long-press to rename or erase.
The diary will open without a code. It stays encrypted on the phone.
Turn the wheels and tap “Lock in”.
Code: %s.\n\nIt can\'t be reset or recovered. If it\'s forgotten, the diary can only be erased together with everything written in it.
The code can\'t be reset: without it the writing can\'t be decrypted. The only option is to erase this diary completely and start a new one.
All days, photos, voice notes and the cover will be gone forever. This can\'t be undone (except from a backup).
The backup is a single file encrypted with this password. Keep it anywhere (USB stick, computer). It can\'t be opened without the password — don\'t forget it.
The diary from the backup will appear on the shelf next to the others (without a lock — set one if needed).
This isn\'t a diary backup, or the file is damaged
Search notes by words, dates and periods.
Days with entries are circled. Tap one to turn to it.
Black glass, clean lines, a soft glow
While the ink is fresh, the text can be edited freely. Dry ink can\'t be changed — only crossed out (you can always add more).
Clock and battery — only by swiping down

Take a page with your finger in its outer third (not at the very edge — that's the phone's back gesture) and pull: right to left — forward, left to right — back. Let go halfway and the page either settles or falls back, like a real one. The cover turns the same way, only heavier.

The faint arrow that appears in the bottom corner after a moment is a hint: you can turn further this way.

The diary opens at today (or at its first page — as chosen in its settings).

The phone's back gesture closes the diary to the cover, once more — to the shelf. The bottom bar (pen, canvas, photo, voice, shelf) shows up after a touch.

Tap a line — the keyboard appears and the whole book slides above it: the text never leaves the paper.

A day has as many pages as it needs: when a page is full, the diary turns to the next one by itself and you keep writing. New text always goes after what's written.

The first page of a day has spaces for a photo, voice and a drawing (dashed while empty). They can be turned off in the diary's settings.

Place (top right) — tap and write it in. A new day takes the place from the previous one (this can be turned off too).

The pen (icon in the bottom bar) — draw right over the page: underline, strike out with a marker, circle, add a little heart. You can always do this, on any page.

Drawing of the day — a separate canvas sheet: tap the “Drawing of the day” space on the first page. What you drew shows there as a thumbnail; tap it to turn to the canvas, swipe it left to remove it.

The tool follows your finger like a touchpad cursor: move anywhere, and to draw — hold your finger still for a moment. Double-tap — the tool stays down. Near an edge it turns by itself so you can see it.

Pencil, brush, spray, marker, eraser; width, opacity, shapes, smoothing, paint within an outline, stencil. Favourites palette — hold a colour or a tool and it goes onto the board above the bar.

All the details — the “i” button on the pen bar.

Fresh ink is bright and the text can be corrected. The next day it dries: it gets a little duller, and the text, photo and voice can no longer change. You can always draw — drawings never dry.

Dry text can only be crossed out: hold a finger on a word and slide along the line. In “Sheet” the words are struck through with pencil; in “Glass” a frosted glass drop covers them.

To tear out a page: hold the bottom left corner and pull up. It's forever, no undo — only a stub stays at the spine.

Photo of the day — the photo icon in the bottom bar or the space on the page: camera or gallery. One photo per day; it becomes part of the page — black-and-white under glass in “Glass”, a pencil sketch in “Sheet”. Tap the photo to see it bigger; that's also where you caption, replace or remove it.

Recording of the day — the microphone in the bottom bar or the plate on the page opens the tape recorder. One cassette per day, sides A and B of 45 minutes each; a new recording is added to the end. Tap the cassette to turn it over.

To remove a photo, the cassette or an empty space right from the page — swipe it left (you can undo at once). The text takes the freed room.

Search — the ribbon at the top of the page: pull it down. Words, numbers, dates, months, years, place, and “week”, “month”, “year”. Tap a result — the diary turns to that day and highlights the word. Photos and Audio — only photos (with a slideshow) or only recordings.

The calendar icon next to the search field: month pages, days with entries are circled.

If something was written on this day a year (or more) ago, today's page has a folded corner at the bottom.

The diary's settings (long-press the spine) → “Set a lock”: turn the four dials and confirm. From then on the diary opens only with this code — the dials are right on the cover. After several wrong tries in a row you'll have to wait a little.

The code can't be reset or recovered. If it's forgotten, the diary can only be erased.

Everything written is always encrypted (even without a lock). While a locked diary is open, screenshots are off; as soon as the app goes to the background, it closes.

The shelf icon at the bottom of a diary leads to the shelf with spines. Tap a spine to take the diary out; long-press it for its settings: cover, name, lock, delete, and, on the next page, what the pages hold.\n\nThe gear at the bottom of the shelf — general settings: guide, new diary, backup, style, language, screen; on the next page — all diaries in a list.

The gear on the shelf → “Back up all diaries”: every diary (days, drawings, photos, voice, covers) goes into one file encrypted with a password you choose. A locked diary is included only if you enter its code.

The password can't be recovered — without it nobody can open the file, you included.

On a new phone: the gear on the shelf → “Restore from backup”, pick the file and enter the password. The diaries go onto the shelf without locks — set them again if needed.
No room for a photo — shorten this day\'s text
No room for a recording — shorten this day\'s text
Off — the whole page is for text
Off — the recording space goes to text
Drag your finger over dry words to strike them out. Tap the icon again to leave
This day already has a recording — swipe it left to record a new one
Tear out the page — forever, no way back
The page has dried — you can still draw
Ink dries after a day: then the page can\'t be changed — no text, photo or voice. The pencil stays, or the page can be torn out (hold the bottom-left corner and drag up).
Tap a diary to open its own settings (cover, name, lock, photos and voice, backup).
The diary is locked — its settings appear once you open it with the code
All photos of the last week
One random photo from each week of the month
One random photo from each month of the year
Only photos: by words from the notes, dates and periods. Ask for the best — one photo from each part of the period.
Only recordings: by words from the notes, dates and periods.
Carry the place to the next day
A new page takes the place from the previous one. Turn off for a travel diary
Allow the camera to take a photo of the day
This side of the cassette is full (45 minutes) — turn it over to side B.
Off — the diary opens at its first page
Canvas — a blank sheet to draw on
The canvas and everything drawn on it will be removed.
Hold at the end — the shape straightens
Paint stays on its side of an outline: start inside — only inside, outside — only around it
Stencil: the pencil draws a film, not a line

Moving
• The cursor works like a touchpad: slide anywhere, the tool follows. Slow — more precise, fast — further.
• Hold your finger for a moment — the tool lowers and draws; lift — it rises.
• Double‑tap — the tool stays down: lift and re‑grip as you like, the line continues. Tap again — it rises.
• Lower and hold still — a dot.
• Two fingers (tool raised) — zoom and move the page.
• A stylus draws directly, with pressure; its eraser end erases.

Tools
• Pencil — lines and shapes.
• Brush — stroke; scrub (wide, back and forth); fill — lower and lift inside a closed outline.
• Spray — airbrush or paint; hold in place — it builds up.
• Marker — translucent, flat tip.
• Eraser — exact, soft (blurred edge) or whole lines.

Drawer (tap the selected tool again)
• Sliders — size and opacity. Under each button — what is selected.
• Shape: freehand; “straighten” — hold at the end and a wobbly circle, frame, triangle or line becomes neat; line, frame, oval — from where you lowered to the tip.
• Smoothing: as drawn, smooth, smoother.
• Inside: start inside an outline — paint stays inside; start outside — only around it.
• Stencil (pencil): draw a film — a wall for paint. “Remove stencil” takes it away, the paint keeps a crisp edge.
• Bin — clear the page.

Colour
• Palette (with black, white and bright ones too), recent colours, eyedropper (picks a colour from the drawing), custom colour — from black to white.

Favourites
• The palette icon on the bar — a paint board above the tools.
• Hold a colour or a tool — it goes onto the palette (a tool with all its settings and colour).
• Tap to take it. Hold it on the palette to remove it.

Other
• Arrows — undo and redo. Tick — finish.
• Drawings never dry: you can draw any time, on old pages too.
• Drawing of the day — a separate canvas sheet: the “Drawing of the day” space on the first page.
A locked diary goes into the backup only with its code. “Cancel” — without it.
Backup saved, but without some locked diaries

This is a paper diary in your phone: a day is a page (and as many more as it takes), and you turn it with your finger like a real one.

You can have several diaries — they stand on a shelf, spines out. Tap a spine to take a diary out.

Everything stays only on this phone and is always encrypted. The diary has no internet access: it sends nothing anywhere and doesn't know where you are. Only you make copies — as a password-protected file (see “Backup”).

Two styles — “Glass” (black glass, straight lines, glow) and “Sheet” (white pencil on old black paper) — are chosen in Settings and apply to all diaries.

A diary's settings — long-press its spine on the shelf.

Cover — a photo from the gallery or camera (it takes on the style's look) or the plain one it had.

“Rename” turns to the cover with the cursor already in the name: type and press Enter. Hold the name and drag to move it (within the upper half, so the keyboard doesn't cover it).

The real cover can't do this — so nothing gets changed by accident.

A diary's (long-press the spine, second page):
• Photos on pages, voice recordings, drawing of the day — when off, their room goes to text.
• Carry the place to the next day — better off for a travel diary.
• Open at today — otherwise at the first page.

General (the gear on the shelf):
• Style — “Glass” or “Sheet”, for all diaries.
• Language — Ukrainian, Polish, English or as on the phone.
• Hide the status bar — clock and battery only with a swipe from the top.
• Vibration — page turns, lock dials, buttons.
Room for a drawing on the first page. You can always draw over the text
